status: frozen before any batch-4 arm has trained; written after the batch-1 readout (receipts/analysis/lucid_expansion_prototype_batch1_20260902.json), which motivates it
question: At a 1.5 ceiling the scalar gate merely matched fixed width (R5 delta +0.003), because 1.5 is safe for a policy that has mastered lambda=1. Does feedback earn its place where the open-loop ceiling is NOT safe? The attribution sweep says push disturbance breaks trained policies at 3x (0.71-0.77 success). fixed_300 trains there blind; gate_300 must stop where its probe fails; box_fast_300 may stop push and keep widening the channels that are still free.

design.origin: same as batch 1 (fixed@s8600 final, sha256 e7fe72a0a48d...)

arms.fixed_300: lambda 3.0 from iteration 0, latency capped at 1.5, single stratum (blind width)
arms.gate_300: scalar probe-gated frontier 1.0 -> <=3.0, step 0.125, window 100 / dwell 50 / min 200 episodes, latency capped 1.5, 8 strata
arms.box_fast_300: per-channel box, ceilings 3.0 on mass/CoM/joint/friction/push and 1.5 on latency, FAST cadence window 50 / dwell 25 / min 100 episodes so a round of six channels takes ~300 iterations; probe budget 300

design.why_the_box_is_a_new_design_not_a_retune: R1 shelved the sequential box at window 100 because its cadence, not its evidence, left it at 1.375; batch 4 changes the cadence and the ceiling, which changes what the arm can express. The R1 verdict on the window-100 box at a 1.5 ceiling stands.
design.driver: tools/run_queue_batch4_20260902.sh (GATE_WINDOW=50 GATE_DWELL=25 GATE_MIN_EPISODES=100 for the box invocation only)

wide_corner.support: inside for whichever channels an arm actually reached beyond 2.5; the realized frontier of every arm is reported next to the score and the cell is LABELLED for each arm rather than assumed held out

held_out_band_150.reading: the batch-1 endpoint, for comparison with fixed_150 / gate_150; in support for all three batch-4 arms on every channel they passed 1.75

endpoints.collapse_check: phys_100 and phys_150 for every arm: a blind 3.0 arm that scores below the origin's 0.994 at phys_100 has been damaged by over-wide training, which is the failure feedback exists to prevent

decision_rules.R8_gate_vs_fixed_wide: delta = wide_corner(gate_300) - wide_corner(fixed_300). >= +0.03: feedback beats blind width where width is unsafe (the first positive claim for feedback in this programme; single seed, screen only). <= -0.03: blind width wins even at 3.0 and the gate stopped too early; report the frontier it stopped at. Else: no difference.
decision_rules.R9_box_vs_gate_wide: delta = wide_corner(box_fast_300) - wide_corner(gate_300), same thresholds; plus per-channel reading: the box's frontier_vector says which channels it stopped and which it widened.
decision_rules.R10_damage: any arm whose phys_100 falls below 0.97 (origin 0.994, paired noise ~1 point at saturation) is flagged DAMAGED; a damaged fixed_300 with an undamaged gate_300 is the mechanism claim even if R8 is flat.
decision_rules.R3: zero applied decreases and zero frontier decreases on every arm and channel
decision_rules.R4: a box that visits < 3 channels or fires < 1 is STALLED, reported as such

noise: paired within-seed SD on a two-cell band ~2.7 points; one seed screens
not_claimed: that 3.0 is the right ceiling (it is the sweep's breaking point for push, chosen to make the blind arm unsafe)
